User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the PlayNite application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

registrationDate.description: Date and time the user registered.

lastLogin.description: Date and time of the user's last login.

profilePictureUrl.description: URL of the user's profile picture.

accessibilitySettings.description: JSON string of accessibility settings for the user. Includes contrast, text size, etc.

gdprConsentDate.description: Date and time the user provided GDPR consent.

Video.title: Video
Video.description: Represents a video in the PlayNite application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the video entity.

uploadDate.description: Date and time the video was uploaded.

duration.description: Duration of the video in seconds.

categoryIds.description: References to Categories. (Relationship: Video N:N Category)

tagIds.description: References to Tags. (Relationship: Video N:N Tag)

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a category for videos in the PlayNite application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category entity.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a tag for videos in the PlayNite application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the tag entity.

Creator.title: Creator
Creator.description: Represents a content creator (non-user uploads) in the PlayNite application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the creator entity.

VideoRating.title: VideoRating
VideoRating.description: Represents a rating given to a video by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the video rating entity.

rating.description: The rating given by the user (e.g., 1-5).

timestamp.description: Date and time the rating was given.

WatchLater.title: WatchLater
WatchLater.description: Represents a video added to a user's 'watch later' list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the watch later entity.

addedDate.description: Date and time the video was added to the 'watch later' list.

Favorite.title: Favorite
Favorite.description: Represents a video added to a user's favorites list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the favorite entity.

addedDate.description: Date and time the video was added to the favorites list.

VideoHistory.title: VideoHistory
VideoHistory.description: Represents a user's video viewing history.

id.description: Unique identifier for the video history entity.

watchDate.description: Date and time the video was watched.

watchPosition.description: The position (in seconds) where the user stopped watching the video.

ReportedVideo.title: ReportedVideo
ReportedVideo.description: Represents a video reported as inappropriate.

id.description: Unique identifier for the reported video entity.

userId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N ReportedVideo). Optional, as reports can be anonymous.

reportDate.description: Date and time the video was reported.

Playlist.title: Playlist
Playlist.description: Represents a custom video playlist created by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the playlist entity.

creationDate.description: Date and time the playlist was created.

PlaylistItem.title: PlaylistItem
PlaylistItem.description: Represents a video within a playlist.

id.description: Unique identifier for the playlist item entity.

itemOrder.description: The order of the video within the playlist.

addedDate.description: Date and time the video was added to the playlist.

ContentPolicy.title: ContentPolicy
ContentPolicy.description: Represents a content policy used for moderation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the content policy entity.

rules.description: JSON string representing the rules of the policy.

ModerationLog.title: ModerationLog
ModerationLog.description: Represents a log entry for content moderation actions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation log entry.

moderationDate.description: Date and time the moderation action was taken.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a notification for a user.

userId.description: The ID of the user who should receive the notification.

message.description: The content of the notification message.

timestamp.description: Date and time the notification was created.

isRead.description: Whether the user has read the notification.

link.description: A URL to navigate to when the notification is clicked.

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: Represents a comment on a video.

videoId.description: The ID of the video the comment belongs to.

userId.description: The ID of the user who posted the comment.

timestamp.description: Date and time the comment was posted.

Follower.title: Follower
Follower.description: Represents a follower relationship between two users.

followerId.description: The ID of the user who is following.

followedId.description: The ID of the user being followed (the creator).

timestamp.description: Date and time the follow action occurred.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to prioritize authorization independence, clarity, and scalability. It utilizes denormalization of authorization data, structural segregation for homogeneous security postures, and consistent access modeling to ensure simple and robust security rules. The structure avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies to allow atomic operations (transactions/batches) and simplifies debugging.

Authorization Independence (CRITICAL): All user-owned data is stored under the `/users/{userId}` path. For collaborative entities, a membership map is denormalized into each document to avoid `get()` calls in security rules.

Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture): Data with different access needs are stored in separate collections (e.g., public videos, user-owned playlists, admin-managed content policies).

Access Modeling (Standardization and Consistency): User-owned data follows the `/users/{userId}/{entityName}/{entityId}` pattern. Collaborative data uses membership maps. Global roles are managed via dedicated collections.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters): The structure supports secure `list` operations by segregating data based on access control requirements and utilizing membership maps for collaborative entities.

Invariants: Ownership is enforced via path-based rules and denormalized data. Timestamps and denormalized data integrity are enforced within security rules.
